source.title: Bodyweight Bar Horizontal rows.  a pull up regression

sourceFacts: Choose doable rep counts at 60% and 80% of a reviewed baseline.
The 80% day uses two-thirds of the 60% day volume; add sets at fixed geometry.
The source gives two days of each type per week and optional 4–6-week maximum retest as an example.
appDecisions: Optional profile for the existing bent-knee row; the default fixed-dose profile and its history identity are unchanged.
A conservative self-reviewed clean baseline (5–200) instead of requiring a maximum test; 0 leaves the optional method inactive.
Floor both rep fractions and higher-rep whole-set volume; reject an explicit lower-rep starting set count that cannot fit even one higher-rep whole set.
Default 2–4 lower-rep sets (3 minimum when rounding requires it), 90-second rests, alternating qualifying tracks and two clean exposures of each before jointly increasing stage. All are app defaults.
Incomplete, changed-setup, painful, failed or reduced work cannot progress the wave. Recovery resets paired evidence and returns to lower-rep practice.
Endpoint maintenance alternates without increasing targets; explicit baseline review/restart creates a separate policy identity, including same-number restarts.
limits: No forced four-day training week, daily maximum, timed automatic retest or guarantee of pull-up readiness.
Grip, foot placement and apparatus safety remain self-confirmed; changing height starts a separate comparison cycle.
Straight-leg, elevated-feet and automatic geometry progression remain unimplemented.

quotes.quote: the 80% should be 2/3 of the volume of the 60% day
after four to 6 weeks you could retest your Max
